body: The asset manager aims to raise around USD 500 million for its third private credit fund and up to USD 300 million for a separate vehicleICICI Prudential Asset Management Company (AMC) is seeking to raise up to USD 800 million through its private credit and special opportunities funds, as demand for alternative investment assets grows among wealthy investors and institutions, according to people familiar with the matter.The Indian asset manager aims to close its third private credit fund at around USD 500 million in December. Separately, it is seeking to raise up to USD 300 million for a special opportunities vehicle, the people said, requesting anonymity because the information is private.The fundraising comes amid the expansion of private credit in Asia, where the segment has so far remained relatively insulated from turmoil affecting other markets. Private credit funds typically have closed-ended structures and limited exposure to software companies, according to the people.Indian asset managers have raised billions of dollars for private credit strategies and are accounting for a growing share of lending transactions in the country. This has increased competition for international investment firms, including Bain Capital and Davidson Kempner Capital Management.Private Credit Fund Attracts Institutional CommitmentsICICI Prudential Corporate Credit Opportunities Fund has secured commitments from more than a dozen insurance companies, alongside family offices and high-net-worth individuals, the people said.The fund focuses on performing credit rather than distressed debt. Its strategy involves providing capital to companies for business expansion and other capital expenditure requirements, they added.The latest fund follows two earlier private credit vehicles launched by ICICI Prudential AMC, which raised around USD 160 million and USD 330 million, respectively, according to the people.The asset manager has deployed capital in companies including GMR Group, Puravankara and Pinnacle Industries, the people said. The companies did not respond to emails seeking comment.ICICI Bank And Prudential BackingICICI Prudential AMC is backed by ICICI Bank and Prudential Plc. Prudential Corp., a subsidiary of the UK-listed insurer, holds approximately one-third of the Indian asset manager.A spokesperson for ICICI Prudential AMC declined to comment on the fundraising plans.
